title: Rocket Report: A rare Falcon 9 scrub; is it just about Vulcan's time to shine?
gist: Weekly launch roundup: ULA's Vulcan targets an Oct 29 return to flight for Amazon Leo with cadence set to rise; SpaceX's 5-year CDS widened to 194bp amid plans for $40B in debt to buy Nvidia chips; Blue Origin is building four New Glenn pads; European launch efforts (Themis, HyImpulse, RFA) keep slipping.

insights.claim: SpaceX plans to raise $40 billion in debt to buy Nvidia chips, and its five-year credit default swap spread rose to 194 basis points, per the Financial Times.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Widening CDS signals credit markets questioning leverage-funded AI capex at SpaceX.
insights.quote: the spread on SpaceX’s five-year credit default swaps rose to 194 basis points on Wednesday
insights.locator: Concerns about credit risks at SpaceX

insights.claim: Apollo was expected to lead the $40 billion debt deal with Pimco among lenders in talks; it follows $25 billion of investment-grade debt in June and an $86 billion IPO.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Private credit is a major funder of AI compute buildout at scale.

insights.claim: The new debt deal suggests Elon Musk is doubling down on his bet on Nvidia's technology.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Continued large GPU demand from SpaceX/xAI supports Nvidia.

insights.claim: ULA's Vulcan has a no-earlier-than October 29 return-to-flight date carrying Amazon Leo, with another Amazon Leo Vulcan mission planned this year, and could see a cadence breakthrough next year if its solid boosters work.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Vulcan reliability determines Amazon Leo deployment pace versus Starlink.

insights.claim: Amazon Leo deliberately contracted ULA, Blue Origin, Arianespace and SpaceX from day one to secure heavy-lift capacity despite the risk.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Badyal
insights.so_what: Launch supply diversification is a strategic necessity for Starlink challengers.
insights.quote: From day one we decided to go with a diverse set of partners to supply us with rockets

insights.claim: ULA infrastructure built with Amazon now lets it process two Vulcan rockets simultaneously in two vehicle integration facilities.
insights.speaker: Rajeev Badyal
insights.so_what: Doubling processing capacity is key to higher launch cadence.

insights.claim: Jeff Bezos said Blue Origin is building three more pads, for four total under construction, alongside a request to the FAA for 50 launches a year from Florida.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Signals heavy infrastructure investment to compete with SpaceX on cadence.
insights.locator: Blue Origin building three more pads

insights.claim: Bezos's stated goal of flying every day, then every hour, then every minute is ambitious for a company that has yet to launch once a month.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Discount Blue Origin's cadence rhetoric versus actual execution.

insights.claim: The EU extended the 42.8 million euro SALTO project deadline to end-2026 for Themis's first hop test, after slipping from an original November 2025 deadline.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Europe's reusable launch effort continues to lag, sustaining dependence on US providers.

insights.claim: HyImpulse pushed its second SR75 suborbital flight to spring 2027, citing licensing and weather at SaxaVord rather than vehicle readiness.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Regulatory licensing is a bottleneck for European launch startups.

insights.claim: Rocket Factory Augsburg named Alexander Dahm CEO as it works toward RFA ONE's debut after losing a first stage in a 2024 static-fire test.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Leadership change at a pre-revenue European launcher.
insights.locator: German launch company gets a new CEO

insights.claim: South Korea's Nuri rocket achieved its fourth consecutive success, raising its success rate to 80 percent, and the government pledged support for private-sector-led launches.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: South Korea is shifting toward a commercial launch industry.

insights.claim: A Falcon 9 for the Space Development Agency scrubbed in the final minute of countdown, a rare event, with the launch slipping to no earlier than October 10.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Minor reliability blip in the dominant launch provider.

insights.claim: Cape Canaveral Space Force Station is getting drone-zapping lasers because traditional RF jamming could damage space vehicles, after hundreds of drone incursions last year.
insights.speaker: Eric Berger
insights.so_what: Demand signal for directed-energy counter-drone systems.
insights.locator: Next step: sharks with laser beams
